CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint of time to CDMS was met with HR 0.663 (p=0.0028), a clinically meaningful delay in conversion from CIS to CDMS. Time to McDonald MS was also strongly significant (HR 0.583, p<0.000001). However, two of the three co-primary endpoints failed: time to confirmed EDSS progression (HR 0.764, p=0.1604) and FAMS TOI at Month 60 (p=0.888). The EDSS progression miss may reflect the early disease stage (CIS population) where disability accumulation is slow and the trial may have been underpowered for this endpoint. The FAMS TOI miss suggests quality-of-life/functional outcomes were not meaningfully different, possibly because the population was early-stage and relatively high-functioning at baseline. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: The KM curves show consistent benefit across years 2, 3, and 5 for CDMS conversion (26.9% vs 45.0% at year 2; 46.2% vs 57.3% at year 5), confirming a durable treatment effect in this CIS population. No differential subgroup responses were formally reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial is adequately powered (n=468), long duration (5 years), and placebo-controlled. The EDSS progression miss is likely due to the early disease stage and low event rate rather than a fundamental mechanism failure. The FAMS TOI miss is consistent with a high-functioning population at baseline where quality of life is preserved regardless of treatment. Overall, the trial is classified as a success based on the pre-specified primary endpoint (time to CDMS) being met with strong statistical and clinical significance, supported by multiple concordant secondary endpoints.
